title: The invite path honours the elicited invite-transport for every option and records the outcome
asA: shelf consumer applying application-admin-console with an invite-transport chosen at elicit time
iWant: the users surface to deliver invites through the elicited transport with a defined success and a defined refusal per option
soThat: the invite control I click never silently misdelivers and every outcome shows up in the audit stream

acceptanceCriteria.description: When invite-transport is `email` and the applied email companion accepts the invite payload, the invite row records data-invite-outcome=accepted and the audit stream carries a row naming transport=email, the invitee and outcome=accepted. Applying agent sets: the email companion binding name, the from address and the invite template id.
acceptanceCriteria.given: invite-transport=email applied and the email companion returns accepted
acceptanceCriteria.when: an admin clicks invite for a pending principal
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invite row exposes data-invite-outcome=accepted and the audit stream row names transport=email, invitee and outcome=accepted

acceptanceCriteria.description: When invite-transport is `email` and the applied email companion rejects the payload (a non-2xx response or a timeout), the invite row shows data-invite-outcome=failed with a retry control, no audit record marks the invite accepted, and the console announces the failure through the notifications live region.
acceptanceCriteria.given: invite-transport=email applied and the companion returns a non-2xx or times out
acceptanceCriteria.then: the invite row carries data-invite-outcome=failed, a data-action=retry-invite control is keyboard-reachable, the audit stream row records outcome=failed and no outcome=accepted row is emitted for this invitee

acceptanceCriteria.description: When invite-transport is `in-app-only`, the invite path never invokes the email companion; the invite writes a notification with data-invite-transport=in-app-only to the applied notification stream, and the users row records data-invite-outcome=recorded.
acceptanceCriteria.when: an admin clicks invite for a pending principal
acceptanceCriteria.then: no email transport is called, the notifications stream carries a row with data-invite-transport=in-app-only, and the users row carries data-invite-outcome=recorded

acceptanceCriteria.description: When invite-transport is `custom` and a project-supplied invite handler is registered on the applied capability sidecar, the invite payload is handed to the handler and success is recorded only after the handler resolves; when no handler is registered the invite refuses at apply-time with INVITE_HANDLER_MISSING naming the sidecar key. Applying agent sets: the handler function name and the sidecar key it registers under.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the handler is called with { invitee, orgId?, correlationId } and the row records data-invite-outcome=accepted only after the handler resolves; a missing handler refuses at apply with INVITE_HANDLER_MISSING

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every transport branch writes exactly one audit-stream row per invite, naming transport, invitee identifier and outcome (accepted, failed or refused). No transport branch writes zero rows or more than one row for a single invite click.
acceptanceCriteria.when: an admin clicks invite once for a principal
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit stream carries exactly one row for this invite naming transport, invitee and outcome
